title: The Withdrawal and Return of the Spouse

blocks.s: Bernard also teaches that even from the perfect the heavenly Spouse long desired and sought, withdraws quickly and eludes — withdrawing from the sublime vision, from contemplation's sweetness, from sensible union. This is not to be grieved over inordinately: he withdraws for their protection, lest they be lifted up by the greatness of consolation, lest constant presence lead them to despise companions, and lest they attribute continuous visitation to nature rather than grace. For common proverb says: Nimia familiaritas parit contemptum — too great familiarity breeds contempt. He withdraws, therefore, lest the too-frequent be despised; that being absent he may be more desired; that being desired he may be more ardently sought; that long sought he may at last be found more gratefully. He permits us to taste a little how sweet he is, and before we fully experience this, he withdraws himself, and so, as it were spreading his wings over us (cf. Deut. 32:11), he provokes us to fly — as if saying: You have tasted a little how gracious and sweet I am; if you wish to be fully satisfied with this sweetness, hasten after me in the fragrance of my ointments, lifting your hearts upward where I am at the right hand of God the Father. There you will see me, not through a glass in a dark manner, but face to face; and your heart shall fully rejoice, and no one shall take your joy from you (cf. John 16:22; 1 Cor. 13:12; Col. 3:1).
